content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text labels the Luke 2:48-49 point UNDERDETERMINED on the basis of how a single verse's phrase is qualified by the next phrase, which is the kind of single-verse non-settlement the rule addresses.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase \"thy father\" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to \"my Father's business.\"","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings, with nothing else settling it, is such a verse.","room":"Phrase: 'does not state a link or its contrary' and 'admits both readings.' Reading (1): the judge may use a single verse's dual/qualified phrases to call the point UNDERDETERMINED; reading (2): K-S2 forbids that unless something else settles it.","why":"The judge's stated reason rests only on Luke 2:48-49's internal 'thy father'/'my Father's business' qualification, so it treats a single verse that does not settle the link as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED, which K-S2 forbids."}
